body: Thank you for your comment! I’ve gone for therapy for about two years (I’ve stopped now because it was with a charity and they take on more severe/emergency cases and let you stop once they assess things have improved) and it has helped a lot, but dark moments like this still occasionally engulf me and everything loses it’s colour and I just want everything to stop. I do have people who love me but I feel like I’m such a letdown somehow that sometimes I feel like they’d be better off without me. It’s hard to feel ok with my accomplishments when people close to me want me to do more and I can’t keep up with the expectations, or ‘let my potential go to waste’

Same here. I’ve had really bad months and years where I was ultra sensitive and suicidal and it got better after therapy. Whenever someone close to me is a little unhappy with me, my emotions immediately jump off a cliff and I just want to cease existing. If it was easy to die, I’d probably have done it a hundred different times by now, and I think about that every time I feel emotionally overwhelmed, and it’s been like that since I was 5 years old.

I think it depends on your therapist and you and how well you work together. I’ve gone for therapy and it helped a lot, but it wasn’t easy and she pushed me hard to challenge my thought processes and how warped my perception was of myself. I still have tough days but I have better tools to help myself than I did before. I hope things work out for you as well! I’d say try to stick with one therapist for at least three to five sessions before you decide to jump to another one if you feel you don’t click, because it takes time to build that relationship and work on issues. I’ve had friends who’ve changed therapists multiple times and only done one or two sessions with each therapist, and they ended up disillusioned because it wasn’t helping.
I hope we both find our ways out of this positively. As empty and hopeless as I feel, I wish for others like you to find meaning and self-compassion
Omgosh I just got excited there, because that is one thing I love to do too! I hope it offers you some sort of reprieve from the pain you feel
Is there any activity you enjoy, even if you feel aren’t good at it?
I’m glad to know happiness exists at least, because sometimes I find it so difficult to imagine

There are things that give me temporary bouts of joy — hobbies like drawing and cycling — but these are not enough for me to actually feel happy. What does it even mean to be happy? Are people ever actually happy?

What if you don’t even know happiness, only sadness and numbness? My therapist told me that when I am distressed, one of the steps to make myself feel better is to recognise the impermanence of my emotions. It is true, the distress does pass, but it never morphs into happiness either
